name: Landscape objects, two dimensions
description: Four nuclides moving through three landscape objects. Compartments are indexed by Radionuclides x Object, so each box on the diagram is really 12 state variables. Sorption is per nuclide, discharge is per object, and the Wetland sub-set drains only the lake and the mire. The three reductions show the two ways of collapsing a dimension: Inventory adds two blocks index by index, TotalWater sums one block over the nuclides, and PeakObject takes the largest object for each nuclide. Solved with the NDF solver, which handles the stiffness from Pb-210 and Ra-226 in a fraction of the steps the Rosenbrock pair needs.

parameters.name: Kd
parameters.comment: Sorption: nuclide specific, shared across objects

parameters.name: discharge
parameters.comment: Water turnover: object specific, shared across nuclides

parameters.name: rho
parameters.comment: Bulk density of the solid, in the retardation factor.

parameters.name: porosity
parameters.comment: Water-filled porosity, in the retardation factor.

transfers.name: Discharge
transfers.comment: Every object discharges into the one downstream compartment, so this flux is summed over Object on the way in. That is what sum_extra_indices asks for; without it the model is refused, because a flux whose ends do not correspond is far more often a mistake than an intention.

transfers.name: WetlandLoss
transfers.comment: Only the wetlands lose water this way; the forest does not. Indexed by Radionuclides x Wetland, and the Wetland sub-set resolves onto the Object dimension of the compartments.

index_reductions.name: TotalWater
index_reductions.comment: Every nuclide in the water of each object -- the sum this used to spell out by hand.

index_reductions.name: PeakObject
index_reductions.comment: The worst object for each nuclide.

block_reductions.name: Inventory
block_reductions.comment: Regolith and water together, object by object.
